questions.question:
The transistor shunt regulator
shown in figure has a
regulated output voltage of 10
V, when the input varies from
20 V to 30 V. The relevant
parameters for the Zener diode
and the transistor are: [latex]V_{Z}[/latex]
=9.5,[latex]V_{SE}[/latex] =0.3V, [latex]\beta[/latex]
=99. Neglect
the current through [latex]R_{B}[/latex]. Then
the maximum power dissipated
in the Zener diode ([latex]P_{Z}[/latex]) and the
transistor ([latex]P_{T}[/latex]) are
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} I_{1 \max }&=\frac{V_{\text {in } \max }-V_{O}}{20}\\ I_{1} &=\frac{30-10}{20}=1 \mathrm{A} \quad \text { (i.e. when } I_{Z}=0) \\ I_{E} &=I_{C}+I_{Z} &\ldots(i)\\ I_{B} &=I_{Z}\left(\text { as no current flows in } R_{B}\text { ) } \right.\\ \beta &=\frac{I_{C}}{I_{B}}=\frac{I_{C}}{I_{Z}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad I_{C} &=\beta I_{Z} \\ \text { From (i) }, I_{E} &=\beta I_{Z}+I_{Z}=(99+1) I_{Z} \\ I_{E} &=100 I_{Z} \\ I_{1} &=I_{E}=100 I_{Z} \\ I_{Z} &=\frac{I_{1}}{100}=\frac{1}{100}=0.01 \mathrm{A} \\ P_{Z} &=V_{Z} I_{Z}=9.5 \times 0.01=95 \mathrm{mW} \\ I_{C} &=99 I_{Z}=99 \times 0.01=0.99 \mathrm{A} \\ P_{C} &=V_{C} I_{C}=10 \times 0.99=9.9 \mathrm{W}\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} I_{1 \max }&=\frac{V_{\text {in } \max }-V_{O}}{20}\\ I_{1} &=\frac{30-10}{20}=1 \mathrm{A} \quad \text { (i.e. when } I_{Z}=0) \\ I_{E} &=I_{C}+I_{Z} &\ldots(i)\\ I_{B} &=I_{Z}\left(\text { as no current flows in } R_{B}\text { ) } \right.\\ \beta &=\frac{I_{C}}{I_{B}}=\frac{I_{C}}{I_{Z}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad I_{C} &=\beta I_{Z} \\ \text { From (i) }, I_{E} &=\beta I_{Z}+I_{Z}=(99+1) I_{Z} \\ I_{E} &=100 I_{Z} \\ I_{1} &=I_{E}=100 I_{Z} \\ I_{Z} &=\frac{I_{1}}{100}=\frac{1}{100}=0.01 \mathrm{A} \\ P_{Z} &=V_{Z} I_{Z}=9.5 \times 0.01=95 \mathrm{mW} \\ I_{C} &=99 I_{Z}=99 \times 0.01=0.99 \mathrm{A} \\ P_{C} &=V_{C} I_{C}=10 \times 0.99=9.9 \mathrm{W}\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: In the DRAM cell in figure, the [latex]V_{t}[/latex] of the NMOSFET is 1 V. For the following three combinations of WL and BL voltages.

An electrical system and its signal-flow graph representations are shown in figure
 (a) and (b) respectively. The values of [latex]G_{2}[/latex] and H, respectively are
questions.explanation: From KVL in both loops In first loop, [latex] V_{i}(s)=I_{1}(s) Z_{1}(s)+\left[I_{1}(s)-I_{2}(s)\right] Z_{3}(s) [/latex] [latex] V_{i}(s)=I_{1}(s)\left[Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)\right]-I_{2}(s) Z_{3}(s) [/latex] [latex] \frac{V_{i}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)}=I_{1}(s)-\frac{I_{2}(s) \cdot Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)} \; \; ...(i)[/latex] In second loop, [latex] \left[I_{2}(s)-I_{1}(s)\right] Z_{3}(s)+I_{2}(s) Z_{2}(s)+I_{2}(s) Z_{4}(s)=0 [/latex] [latex] I_{2}(s)\left(Z_{2}(s)+Z_{3}(s)+Z_{4}(s)\right)=I_{1}(s) \cdot Z_{3}(s) [/latex] [latex] G_{2}=\frac{I_{2}(s)}{I_{1}(s)}=\frac{Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{2}(s)+Z_{3}(s)+Z_{4}(s)} [/latex] From SFG, [latex]I_{1}(s)=V_{i} G_{1}(s)+I_{2}(s) H(s) [/latex] [latex] I_{1}(s)=V_{i}(s) \frac{1}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)}+I_{2}(s) \frac{Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)} [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad H(s)=\frac{Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)} [/latex] (comparing above two equations)
questions.explanation_html:
From KVL in both loops In first loop,
[latex] V_{i}(s)=I_{1}(s) Z_{1}(s)+\left[I_{1}(s)-I_{2}(s)\right] Z_{3}(s) [/latex]
[latex] V_{i}(s)=I_{1}(s)\left[Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)\right]-I_{2}(s) Z_{3}(s) [/latex]
[latex] \frac{V_{i}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)}=I_{1}(s)-\frac{I_{2}(s) \cdot Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)} \; \; ...(i)[/latex]
In second loop,
[latex] \left[I_{2}(s)-I_{1}(s)\right] Z_{3}(s)+I_{2}(s) Z_{2}(s)+I_{2}(s) Z_{4}(s)=0 [/latex]
[latex] I_{2}(s)\left(Z_{2}(s)+Z_{3}(s)+Z_{4}(s)\right)=I_{1}(s) \cdot Z_{3}(s) [/latex]
[latex] G_{2}=\frac{I_{2}(s)}{I_{1}(s)}=\frac{Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{2}(s)+Z_{3}(s)+Z_{4}(s)} [/latex]
From SFG, [latex]I_{1}(s)=V_{i} G_{1}(s)+I_{2}(s) H(s) [/latex]
[latex] I_{1}(s)=V_{i}(s) \frac{1}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)}+I_{2}(s) \frac{Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)} [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad H(s)=\frac{Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)} [/latex]
(comparing above two equations)

questions.question:
The open-loop DC gain of a unity negative feedback system with closed-loop
transfer function [latex]\frac{s+4}{s^{2}+7s+13}[/latex] is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CLTF} &=\frac{G(s)}{1+G(s) H(s)}=\frac{s+4}{s^{2}+7 s+13} \\ \frac{1+G(s) H(s)}{G(s)} &=\frac{s^{2}+7 s+13}{s+4} \end{aligned} [/latex] [latex] H(s)=1[/latex] for unity feedback. [latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{1}{G(s)} &=\frac{s^{2}+7 s+13}{s+4}-1 \\ \frac{1}{G(s)} &=\frac{s^{2}+6 s+9}{s+4} \\ \therefore \quad G(s) &=\frac{s+4}{s^{2}+6 s+9} \\ \text { For D.C. } \quad s&=0\\ \therefore \quad G(s) &=\text{open loop gain} \\ &=\frac{4}{9} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CLTF} &=\frac{G(s)}{1+G(s) H(s)}=\frac{s+4}{s^{2}+7 s+13} \\ \frac{1+G(s) H(s)}{G(s)} &=\frac{s^{2}+7 s+13}{s+4} \end{aligned} [/latex]
[latex] H(s)=1[/latex] for unity feedback.

A material has conductivity of [latex]10^{-2}[/latex]
 mho/m and a relative permittivity of 4. The
frequency at which the conduction current in the medium is equal to the
displacement current is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} |\sigma E| &=|j \omega \in E| \\ \sigma &=2 \pi f \epsilon_{0} \epsilon_{r} \\ \Rightarrow \quad f &=\frac{\sigma}{2 \pi \times \epsilon_{0} \epsilon_{r}} \\ &=\frac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 2 \times 10^{-2}}{4} \\ f &=45 \times 10^{6}=45 \mathrm{MHz} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question:
A uniform plane electromagnetic wave incident normally on a plane surface of a
dielectric material is reflected with a VSWR of 3. What is the percentage of
incident power that is reflected?
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} s&=\frac{1+|\Gamma|}{1-|\Gamma|} \\ \Rightarrow 3&=\frac{1+|\Gamma|}{1-|\Gamma|} \\ |\Gamma|&=0.5 \\ \frac{P_{r}}{P_{i}}&=|\Gamma|^{2}=0.25 \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad 25 \% [/latex] of incident power is reflected.
